name: FSH / Menopur (HMG)

card.summary: Fertility gonadotropins (FSH, hMG) from IVF medicine, discussed in TRT circles as a way to keep sperm production going; the evidence is in women's fertility, not appearance.
card.aka: Menopur, menotropin, human menopausal gonadotropin, hMG, Pergonal
card.note: Prescription fertility drugs with monitoring requirements; trial evidence is mostly in women undergoing IVF.

quick.overview:
Menopur is a brand of highly purified menotropin (human menopausal gonadotropin, hMG), a mixture of FSH and LH activity originally extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women. It is used to stimulate the ovaries in fertility treatment, and the same drug class can be used in hypogonadal men to stimulate sperm production.

In looksmaxxing and TRT communities these gonadotropins come up as fertility-preserving companions to testosterone therapy. The published trials are almost all in women having IVF, and none examine appearance outcomes.
quick.mechanism: FSH acts on ovarian follicles in women and on Sertoli cells in men to support gamete production, while LH activity stimulates sex-hormone production. Menopur supplies both activities; recombinant FSH products supply FSH alone.
quick.risks: Known concerns in women's fertility treatment include ovarian overstimulation and multiple pregnancy. These are prescription drugs given by injection under monitoring. Specific harms in men using them alongside testosterone are not covered by the trials listed here.

lead: Menotropin, also called human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG), is a fertility drug extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women, whose urine is rich in FSH and LH [1]. Menopur, made by Ferring, is a highly purified preparation; earlier products included Pergonal [1].

The extraction method was developed by Piero Donini in 1949 and brought into clinical use by Bruno Lunenfeld in 1961 [1]. Wikipedia notes recombinant FSH has largely replaced hMG in many settings and that a Cochrane analysis found no major clinical outcome differences between urinary and recombinant FSH [1].

Trial evidence is concentrated in women undergoing IVF or ovulation induction [2][3][4]. The 'FSH' entry in this wiki reflects use of gonadotropins in men on testosterone therapy, a use for which the sources reviewed contain no trial data on appearance outcomes.

paras: In women it is used to stimulate follicle growth for IVF and ovulation induction, with daily injections over roughly ten days under close monitoring [1]. In hypogonadal men it can be used to stimulate sperm production [1]. A case report describes a birth after testicular sperm extraction in a man with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism [8].

A randomised, assessor-blind multinational trial in 731 women compared highly purified hMG (Menopur) with recombinant FSH (Gonal-F) in IVF, reporting ongoing pregnancy rates of 27 percent with hMG versus 22 percent with rFSH [5]. A companion analysis examined embryo quality [5]. A trial in poor responders compared 450 IU and 600 IU gonadotropin dosing [6], and a randomised trial compared low-dose hMG with clomiphene in subfertile couples having intrauterine insemination [7]. Economic evaluations of two large trials compared hMG and rFSH costs [9].

Urinary preparations contain impurities in addition to gonadotropins, which has been analysed in the literature [10]. Studies have also compared batch-to-batch consistency of human-derived and recombinant gonadotropin products [11].

Large trials in women show comparative outcomes between hMG and rFSH in IVF [5][12], with additional Phase 3 and 4 registrations of Menopur in infertility, including a 270-patient IVF safety and efficacy study [13] and a 620-patient single-blastocyst transfer study in high responders [14]. No studies found examining FSH or hMG for appearance outcomes or for men using them alongside testosterone therapy.

timeline.event: Piero Donini develops an extraction method for urinary gonadotropins [1].
Bruno Lunenfeld introduces hMG into clinical use [1].
